name: Charles
tagline: A Berlin conversational-commerce platform born from a sustainable fashion brand's own WhatsApp marketing software, now backed by Salesforce Ventures and priced for six-figure annual budgets.
tldr: Charles was founded in Berlin (reported as either 2018 or 2019 across sources) by Artjem Weissbeck (a Kapten & Son co-founder) and Andreas Tussing (an ex-McKinsey ecommerce lead), who originally started Charles as a sustainable fashion brand and built the WhatsApp marketing software in-house before finding no existing tool met their needs — then pivoted to sell the software itself.
Funding is substantial: a $6.5M seed round in 2021, a $20M Series A in 2022 led by Salesforce Ventures with Accel and HV Capital participating, and $30.2M total raised across 4 rounds.

Pricing is entirely custom-quoted with no public pricing page — third-party estimates put entry costs around €349/month plus variable usage costs, but Charles is explicitly positioned for companies planning six-figure annual conversational-commerce budgets, with 'pricier side' being a specific, repeated independent-review complaint.

The AI layer is genuinely well-built for grounding: brands upload FAQs, product feeds, or other data as the agent's explicit knowledge source, and the AI is documented as treating that uploaded content as its source of truth rather than answering from general knowledge.

Integration depth is a real strength, unsurprising given Salesforce Ventures' investment — Shopify, Salesforce, Emarsys, Klaviyo, and Zendesk are all documented integrations enabling live data sync, campaign triggers, and unified analytics across a brand's existing marketing and CRM stack.

Best for established ecommerce and retail brands with real budget for enterprise conversational commerce and a Salesforce- or Klaviyo-centric marketing stack — not for small businesses or anyone needing transparent, self-service pricing.
keyFeatures: AI agents trained on uploaded FAQs, product feeds, or other business data, treating that content as their source of truth rather than answering from general knowledge
Asynchronous two-way WhatsApp communication combined with bulk broadcast messaging for marketing campaigns
Deep native integrations with Shopify, Salesforce, Emarsys, and Klaviyo for live customer-data sync and campaign triggering
A Zendesk integration supporting omnichannel customer-service strategies alongside the core WhatsApp commerce flow
Workflow automation for tailored, trigger-based customer journeys across the connected marketing stack
Live, bidirectional data sharing between Charles and connected shop, CRM/CDP, and service tools, set up in a documented few-click process
Unified analytics spanning connected tools rather than siloed WhatsApp-only reporting
A dedicated success-management and onboarding function, specifically praised by independent reviewers for ongoing support quality

faq.question: Why does Charles have a fashion-brand origin story?
faq.answer: Charles's founders originally started the company as a sustainable fashion brand and wanted to use WhatsApp as their principal marketing channel — when no existing software met their needs, they built it themselves. Only after finding real success with that internal tool did they pivot the business to sell the software to other ecommerce and retail brands. It's a genuine 'built it for ourselves first' origin, similar in spirit to other founder-market-fit stories in this category.

faq.question: How much does Charles actually cost?
faq.answer: There's no public pricing page — every quote is custom. Third-party estimates put entry costs around €349/month plus variable usage-based costs, but Charles is explicitly positioned for companies planning six-figure annual budgets for conversational commerce, and 'pricier side' is a specific, repeated complaint in independent reviews. This is enterprise pricing, not a self-service SaaS tier.

faq.question: How does Charles's AI avoid making things up?
faq.answer: Brands upload FAQs, product feeds, or other business data as the agent's explicit knowledge source, and Charles documents the AI as treating that uploaded content as its source of truth — a real, deliberate grounding mechanism rather than letting the model answer from general knowledge. No independently audited resolution-rate figure exists to verify how well this performs in practice, but the design intent is sound.

faq.question: Why did Salesforce invest in Charles?
faq.answer: Salesforce Ventures led Charles's $20M Series A in 2022, consistent with the platform's genuinely deep Salesforce integration — live customer-data sync, campaign triggers, and unified analytics across a brand's existing CRM. If your business runs on Salesforce, this is one of the more credible, strategically-backed WhatsApp commerce integrations in this category.

faq.question: What's the most common complaint about Charles?
faq.answer: Beyond pricing, independent reviewers specifically flag that analytics for campaigns, customer insights, and flows 'still needs some development' — a real, specific limitation rather than a vague complaint. Separately, reviewers note WhatsApp's own 24-hour conversation-window policy as a cost consideration: a new paid conversation window opens once 24 hours pass without a response, which affects total cost regardless of which platform you use.

faq.question: Does Charles work well for teams already using Klaviyo?
faq.answer: Yes — a documented Klaviyo integration lets brands connect WhatsApp marketing with email marketing for a coordinated multi-channel retention and acquisition strategy, specifically praised in independent reviews as an effective combination for brands already invested in Klaviyo's ecosystem.

pricingBreakdown: Charles doesn't publish pricing at all, and third-party estimates that place an entry point around €349/month plus variable costs likely understate what a real deployment costs, since the company's own positioning explicitly targets six-figure annual budgets. This is squarely enterprise software pricing, consistent with its Salesforce Ventures backing and its integration depth across Shopify, Salesforce, Emarsys, and Klaviyo. Independent reviewers specifically and repeatedly describe the product as being on the pricier side of the category, which tracks with this positioning rather than contradicting it. If you're evaluating Charles, expect a genuine enterprise sales process rather than a self-service signup, and factor in that WhatsApp's own 24-hour conversation-window billing policy — a new paid conversation window opens after 24 hours without a response — applies on top of whatever Charles itself charges, a cost dynamic independent reviewers specifically flag as worth understanding upfront.

verdict: Charles has one of the more genuinely credible founder-market-fit stories in this category: built first to solve its founders' own WhatsApp marketing needs at their sustainable fashion brand, only commercialized once that internal tool proved to work, and now backed by a Series A that Salesforce Ventures itself chose to lead. That strategic backing tracks directly with what the product actually does well — genuinely deep native integrations with Shopify, Salesforce, Emarsys, and Klaviyo that let a brand's existing marketing and CRM stack talk to WhatsApp in real time, not just a bolted-on messaging widget. The AI's knowledge-grounding design is similarly considered: brands explicitly upload FAQs and product feeds as a defined source of truth, a more deliberate approach to hallucination risk than many competitors document, even without an independent benchmark to confirm how well it performs. Where Charles asks the most of a buyer is price and access: there's no public pricing page at all, the company explicitly targets six-figure annual budgets, and independent reviewers specifically and repeatedly describe it as being on the pricier side — this is enterprise software, full stop, not a tool to casually trial. Analytics is the other honest gap, with reviewers directly stating campaign and customer-insight reporting needs further development. My honest read: if you're an established ecommerce or retail brand already invested in Salesforce or Klaviyo, with the budget this tier of tool assumes, Charles's integration depth and thoughtful AI design are genuinely worth an enterprise evaluation. If you need transparent, accessible pricing or deep analytics out of the box, this isn't built for that buyer.
